name: Uffizi Gallery
description: The great collection of Italian Renaissance painting, in the Medici’s former offices by the Arno: Botticelli, Leonardo, Michelangelo and more.

name: Museo Galileo
description: A science museum with the Medici’s scientific instruments, globes and maps, and Galileo’s own telescopes.

name: Florence Cathedral
places: Duomo central doorway, facing the Baptistery
description: The cathedral with Brunelleschi’s dome, its bell tower and the octagonal Baptistery, around the square at the heart of the city.

name: Museo dell’Opera del Duomo
description: The cathedral museum, holding the original Baptistery doors, sculpture from the cathedral and Michelangelo’s late Pietà.

name: Piazza della Signoria
places: Loggia dei Lanzi, Piazza della Signoria
description: Florence’s main civic square, with the Neptune fountain, a copy of Michelangelo’s David, and statues in the open-air Loggia dei Lanzi.

name: Palazzo Vecchio
places: Hall of the Five Hundred, Palazzo Vecchio
description: The fortress-like town hall on Piazza della Signoria, with painted state rooms including the vast Hall of the Five Hundred.

name: Piazza della Repubblica
description: A big 19th-century square on the site of the Roman forum, with a carousel, a triumphal arch and old cafés.

name: Palazzo Medici Riccardi
description: The Medici family’s 15th-century palace, with a small chapel covered in frescoes of the procession of the Magi.

name: Orsanmichele
description: A former grain market turned church, with statues of patron saints in niches on its outside walls, made for the city’s guilds.

name: San Lorenzo
description: The Medici family’s parish church, designed by Brunelleschi, with a bare unfinished facade and the Old Sacristy inside.

name: Laurentian Library
description: The Medici library in the cloister of San Lorenzo, designed by Michelangelo, with a sculptural staircase and a long reading room.

name: Medici Chapels
description: The Medici family tombs behind San Lorenzo, including Michelangelo’s New Sacristy, with a room below where he may have hidden in 1530.

name: Santa Croce
description: A large Franciscan church with the tombs of Michelangelo, Galileo and Machiavelli, the Pazzi Chapel, and a square in front.

name: Bargello Museum
description: A medieval palace and former prison, now Florence’s museum of Renaissance sculpture, with works by Donatello and Michelangelo.

name: Ponte Vecchio
description: A medieval bridge over the Arno lined with jewellers’ shops, with the Vasari Corridor, a private Medici passage, running along the top.

name: Piazzale Michelangelo
description: A hilltop square across the Arno with a wide view over the city and a bronze copy of David.

name: Accademia Gallery
description: The museum that holds Michelangelo’s David, along with his unfinished Prisoners and Florentine paintings.

name: Palazzo Pitti
description: A huge palace across the Arno that became the Medici’s home, now a group of museums, with the Boboli Gardens behind.

name: Santa Maria Novella
description: A Dominican church near the station with a striped marble facade, frescoes and Masaccio’s Trinity, facing its own square.

name: Brancacci Chapel
places: Brancacci Chapel, Santa Maria del Carmine
description: A chapel in the church of Santa Maria del Carmine, covered in early Renaissance frescoes by Masaccio and Masolino.

name: Santo Spirito
description: A Brunelleschi church in the Oltrarno with a plain facade, a wooden crucifix attributed to Michelangelo, and a lively square in front.
